{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Legal review of the Garman Software License and Maintenance Agreement — verified findings and redline positions 
**Prefix for margin comments:** [Playbook]

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement. Of the 19 findings, **6 items are compliant** and require no redline, **11 are deviations** from our playbook, and **2 are missing protections** we have inserted.

Three issues are critical and drive our negotiation:

- **No monetary liability cap at all (§ 15).** Section 15 is mutual on indirect/consequential damages and carves out Sections 13 and 14, but there is no aggregate cap, so both parties — including us — carry unlimited exposure for direct damages, and the "exclusive remedy" wording may cut across warranty remedies. We have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims (confidentiality, IP indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the cap and payment obligations excluded from "damages".
- **Ownership of our data and of paid-for Modifications (§ 13).** Garman retaining its platform IP is acceptable, but Modifications and Improvements we commission and pay for under Schedule "D" vest solely in Garman with no licence back beyond the object-code licence, and the Agreement nowhere confirms our data (including data converted under Section 4) remains ours. We have added a data-ownership sentence, a perpetual royalty-free licence to paid-for Modifications/Improvements, and a no-joint-ownership statement.
- **Narrow indemnity (Page 6).** The IP indemnity is helpfully outside the Section 15 limitation and includes procure/modify/replace remedies, but it is limited to breach of the IP ownership warranty, with no cover for breach of law, data compromise or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, and an unqualified ten-day notice condition. We have added the missing heads and a material-prejudice qualifier.

Secondary but material: the licence grant does not reach our contractors and is non-transferable (so it would not survive an M&A transaction); the assignment bar is absolute with no affiliate or successor carve-out; termination for convenience requires 90 days' notice with no refund of prepaid fees; there is no transition assistance or data-return obligation; renewal mechanics and pricing are undefined; Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** rather than a narrow non-solicit; governing law is Nova Scotia; and there is no insurance covenant despite Garman working on our systems.

Helpfully, the Agreement contains **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no liquidated damages or exit charges, and no audit right against us** — and the only examination right (over the escrowed Codes) runs in our favour.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Page 6 | Broaden Garman indemnity beyond IP title (breach of law, data compromise, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and soften the ten-day notice condition with a material-prejudice qualifier. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Confirm we own our data (including data converted under Section 4); perpetual royalty-free licence back to paid-for Modifications/Improvements; no joint ownership. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | Add mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000, with Excluded Claims outside the cap and payment obligations excluded from "damages". |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Page 10 | Add affiliate/successor carve-out for us; reasonableness standard for other assignments; confirm change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right (none currently in § 17). |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No redline. Licence is expressly non-exclusive; §§ 10 and 11 impose no sole-source obligation. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No redline. No penalties, late-payment interest, early-termination or accelerated fees; refunds in §§ 8 and 17(c) run in our favour. |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 Grant of License | Extend grant to contractors/outsourcers acting for us; make it irrevocable and transferable to a successor (affiliates currently covered only at Authorized Locations). |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Page 2 | No redline. §§ 3 and 20 contain only ordinary licence-scope limits (no service-bureau use, no reverse engineering). |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 17 Term and Termination | Shorten our convenience notice from 90 to 30 days and add pro-rata refund of prepaid licence and maintenance fees. Fallback: 60–90 days with refund. Garman has no convenience right (good). |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No redline. No audit, inspection or usage-verification right against us anywhere in the Agreement. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | Page 10 | Replace Nova Scotia with New York law and the courts of New York County. Fallbacks: Delaware, California, England and Wales. No arbitration clause. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No redline. Fees fixed by Schedule "A"; no pricing-parity language. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No redline to the body. **Confirm Schedule "A" contains no multi-year committed spend** — Schedules were not attached to the draft reviewed. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Deviation | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Convert the mutual no-hire (currently covering any employee, binding affiliates, surviving under § 18) into a narrow non-solicit of personnel actually involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no hiring ban. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Deviation | § 10 Maintenance and Support | Set express 12-month renewals, 30-day non-renewal right, and cap renewal uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% (fallback 5%). Term is presently only "renewable" with no mechanics. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Missing | § 17 Term and Termination | Insert six months' paid transition assistance (fallback 90 days), data return in machine-readable form within 30 days, and certified deletion. Escrow licence in § 16(b) only helps on Garman default. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Duration is acceptable and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer, but no remedy is stated. Add professional-and-workmanlike services warranty (installation, conversion, training, support), no-malicious-code warranty, and repair/replace-then-refund remedy. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | Page 11 | Insert standard covenant in General Matters: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, certificates on request. Fallback: E&O USD 1M, cyber USD 2M. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

We should not sign without movement on the three critical findings:

1. **A mutual monetary cap with Excluded Claims (§ 15).** Unlimited direct-damages exposure on both sides is unacceptable; the current "exclusive remedy" wording must also stop short of our warranty remedies.
2. **Ownership of our data and a licence back to Modifications/Improvements we pay for (§ 13).** We will not pay for development that we cannot use beyond an object-code licence, and our data ownership must be stated expressly.
3. **An indemnity that reaches beyond IP title (Page 6).** Cover for breach of law, data compromise and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus a material-prejudice qualifier on the ten-day notice condition, is required.

On the high-severity items, our clear priorities are the **contractor/successor licence scope (§ 2)** and the **affiliate/successor assignment carve-out (Page 10)**, without which the licence would not survive a corporate transaction.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. Issue the redline with [Playbook] margin comments covering the 11 deviations and 2 missing protections above.
2. Request **Schedules "A" and "D"**, which were not attached to the draft reviewed, and confirm Schedule "A" contains no multi-year committed spend and that Schedule "D" Modifications/Improvements are within the licence-back we have proposed.
3. Table the three critical items (§ 15 cap, § 13 IP/data, Page 6 indemnity) as a package in the first negotiation session, with the stated fallbacks held back.
4. Confirm with the business the acceptable landing zone on convenience notice (30 days sought; 60–90 days with refund as fallback), renewal uplift (3% sought; 5% fallback), transition assistance (six months sought; 90 days fallback) and insurance limits.
5. Confirm with the business that Nova Scotia law and forum is not commercially required before we press the move to New York."}
